text:
sam-ops: Heads up, SIN POP p99 latency jumped from ~90ms -> ~380ms at 04:12 UTC. Throughput fell ~35%. Alerting shows multiple autoscaler scale-ups around that time. :warning:
lee-runtime: Do we see KV-cache miss rate or a batching heuristic flip?
sam-ops: KV miss rate spiked, batching distribution shifted to many tiny batches. Snippet from metrics at 04:12:
```
2026-03-17T04:11:58Z pop=sin batches/sec=320 avg_batch=12 p50=40ms p95=110ms p99=92ms kv_hit=0.88
2026-03-17T04:12:10Z pop=sin batches/sec=900 avg_batch=3  p50=80ms p95=320ms p99=380ms kv_hit=0.55
2026-03-17T04:12:30Z autoscaler=up nodes=+3 churn=true
```
maria-sre: Provider telemetry shows two new hosts on the SIN pool with high steal and occasional CPU capping (noisy VMs flagged). iowait and softirq rose slightly.
ashley-ml: The batcher has a threshold that prefers bigBatch if avg_batch > 8; with sudden node add and many small in-flight requests it flipped to lowLatency path and then back, causing kernel selection oscillation. We saw kernel recompile/reselect logs around the same timestamps.
lee-runtime: Can you dump the kernel selector trace and scheduler stats? Also paste the batching decision log around that window.
sam-ops: Pasted both:
```
[04:12:09] kernel-selector: chosen=fast-path-v2 reason=batch_size=3 latency_target=50
[04:12:11] kernel-selector: selected=conservative-quant reason=probe_fallback
[04:12:12] batcher: heuristic_flip lowLatency->throughput
[04:12:13] kvcache: eviction=0.12 hit=0.55 load_slow=true
```
maria-sre: Host snapshots: one host had cpu.steal ~18% for a 40s window. Provider noted noisy tenant on the same hypervisor. I recommend cordoning those hosts.
ashley-ml: The oscillation amplifies because when batcher flips to low-latency, avg tokens per batch drops -> KV cache warms slower -> more misses -> smaller batches. Feedback loop.
lee-runtime: Agreed. Short-term mitigation: 1) Pin kernel-selector to stable conservative variant on SIN 2) Increase autoscaler cooldown to avoid churn bubble 3) Cordone noisy hosts. Can someone run the kernel pin?
sam-ops: Doing a hotfix now: pin kernel-selector=conservative-2026-02-29 on sin-pop and set autoscaler cooldown to 120s. Rolling to 3 zones.
deploy-bot: deploy started: hotfix/kernel-pin@conservative-2026-02-29 to sin-pop (rollout 15m)
sam-ops: After pin and cordon, p99 dropped to 110ms within 2 mins and throughput recovered to ~95% of nominal. KV hit improved to 0.82.
nashley-ml: I'll add a guard in the batcher to prevent immediate heuristic flips if node count changes within cooldown window. Also will add a synthetic workload in our perf suite to catch this.
maria-sre: I'll file a support case with infra provider about noisy tenant and request placement remediation. Also propose adding host-level steal alarms.
lee-runtime: Action items:
- ashley-ml: perf test + heuristic guard (owner: ashley-ml)
- sam-ops: autoscaler cooldown change persisted and cordon/replace noisy hosts (owner: sam-ops)
- maria-sre: provider case + host alarms (owner: maria-sre)
- lee-runtime: follow up on kernel-selector telemetry and consider making conservative variant default when node churn detected (owner: lee-runtime)

sam-ops: Thanks everyone. Marking this as mitigated for now. Will keep watch and post an update if anything recurs. :thumbsup:
